QF.id: Analysis of Equity and Debt Instruments_1

question.text: Priya exercised ESOPs on 15-Mar-2024 and was allotted 500 listed equity shares at an exercise price of Rs.100 per share. The FMV on the exercise date was Rs.450 per share. She sold all the shares on 20-Apr-2025 at Rs.600 per share. What is the total capital gain arising on the sale?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Level 2 workbook (page 262), for ESOP shares the cost of acquisition for capital-gains purposes is the FMV on the exercise / allotment date, i.e., Rs.450 per share. Capital gain per share = Rs.600 - Rs.450 = Rs.150. Total = 500 x Rs.150 = Rs.75,000. The holding period for capital-gains purposes runs from the share-allotment date on exercise (15-Mar-2024) to the sale date (20-Apr-2025), which is more than 12 months. For listed equity shares with STT paid, that makes the gain Long-Term Capital Gain. The Trap: Rs.2,50,000 uses the exercise price (Rs.100) as cost instead of FMV on exercise (Rs.450). The perquisite component of Rs.350 per share (FMV minus exercise price) is taxed as salary income at the exercise stage; using Rs.100 as cost would double-count that amount. The 'Short-Term' options misapply the holding-period rule for listed shares. Note: ESOP taxation is a two-stage process - perquisite tax at the time of exercise (FMV minus exercise price) and capital gains at the time of sale (sale price minus FMV on exercise). The workbook is careful to distinguish ESOP grant, vesting, exercise, and share-allotment events.
